content.thinking:
I need to avoid writing any figures directly, referencing them only by their labeled names, and start building the causal chain: users experienced slow account pages and elevated errors, which I'll support by citing the relevant error and series graphs.

Tracing further, io-shop's calls to pricing's basket-total endpoint were taking far too long, and affected request volume climbed per the evidence. Restarting the io-pricing dependency restored baseline behavior, but why io-pricing degraded in the first place remains unestablished -- I need to be honest about that gap rather than speculate as fact.

For contributing factors, I'm noting the unclear fix in the proposed pull request, the six-minute delay before the alert fired, a mismatch between the alert text (error rate) and the actual issue (latency), and the apparent absence of a timeout or circuit breaker on io-shop's pricing call -- though that last point is speculative and should be flagged as such.

I'm also weighing whether the recovery happened on its own or because of the restart, since the timestamps coincide but don't prove causation, and noting that the error rate increase was fairly small against an already-elevated baseline. For the executive summary I'm pulling together the incident duration, timestamps, error rates at peak versus before, and the six-minute alert delay. Then I'm drafting three new action items -- starting with one calling for direct latency alerting on the io-pricing dependency so degradation gets caught before it cascades.

Rounding out the remaining action items: investigating why io-pricing slowed before the restart (since the restart wiped useful diagnostic state), and adding timeout/circuit-breaker/fallback protection around the basket-total call in io-shop. I'm also flagging that the alert itself was mislabeled -- named for high latency but describing an error rate -- and deciding whether to fold that into the detection action item. Mapping each contributing factor to its corresponding fix, and noting the lessons: quick dependency identification and confirmed mitigation went well, but late detection and an unexplained root cause did not, and there's a real sense we got lucky that the restart happened to be safe and coincided with recovery.

I need to be careful using the placeholder for the 1500ms figure so it renders correctly without duplicating "ms" or exposing raw digits.

action_items.item: Add an alert on the latency of io-shop's calls to io-pricing, and on io-pricing's own latency, so that dependency slowness pages at onset and names the dependency. Align the HighLatency alert text with what it actually measures.
Investigate why io-pricing slowed down, using its own metrics and logs for the period of the incident. Capture diagnostics such as thread, connection and resource state before any future restart.
Give io-shop's basket-total call to io-pricing a tight timeout, plus a circuit breaker or fallback, so a slow pricing service degrades account pages gracefully instead of stalling them.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw slow account pages and a raised share of failed requests. The paging series rose from {series_before} to {series_at_worst} at its worst, and the error rate peaked at {errors_at_worst}. io-shop logged account-page error-rate warnings and requests failing because shoppers closed the connection.

The account page waited on io-shop's call to the pricing service for the basket total. Each call took {G9feb.1}, and the share of affected requests grew from {G9feb.18} to {G9feb.19} of the sampled {G9feb.2} requests.

The pricing service, io-pricing, was itself degraded. io-shop's own code and config had not changed, there were no production changes, and the flag provider showed no recent flag changes. Restarting io-pricing returned io-shop to its baseline.
Why io-pricing degraded is not shown by the record. Only the log lines on the caller side were read, and no io-pricing diagnostics were collected before the restart. The chain stops here.

contributing_factors.factor: The page came late. The alert was raised {alert_raised - began} after the onset, and it was a latency rule whose text spoke of error rate. Nothing watched the upstream pricing call directly, although its slowness was visible in the logs from the onset.
io-shop has no evident protection against a slow pricing dependency. Every basket-total call waited out the full slow response, and the slowness reached shoppers unchanged.

The cause of io-pricing's degradation is unknown, and the restart may have removed the state that would show it. The same fault could recur without warning. The open proposed fix, AI-2, is not shown to address io-pricing.

input.executive_summary: Shop account pages were slow, and some requests failed, for {duration}, from {began} to {recovered}. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The cause was a slow internal pricing service that the shop depends on. Argus traced the slowness to that service and restarted it, and the shop returned to its normal level. The alert fired {alert_raised - began} after the problem began. The underlying reason the pricing service slowed down has not been established.

got_lucky: The restart fell in the same minute as the recovery, so the record cannot fully separate its effect from a self-recovery of io-pricing. Nothing else was tried, and the restart carried little risk.
went_well: The Investigator tied the latency jump to the slow pricing calls using logs, and it correctly found no change or flag change to blame.
The restart of io-pricing was confirmed against the metrics and left nothing to put back.
went_wrong: The alert was raised {alert_raised - began} after the onset, and its text did not match the rule that fired.
The record does not show why io-pricing degraded, and no diagnostics were taken before the restart.

input.root_cause: io-pricing, which io-shop calls for basket totals, became slow and held each call open for {G9feb.1}, until nearly every such request was affected. Restarting it brought io-shop back to baseline. The record does not show why io-pricing degraded, because no change or flag change preceded it.
input.symptom: Shop account pages were slow and some requests failed
